newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PMs to recall feuding provincial officials.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PMs to recall feuding provincial officials.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen have agreed to replace feuding officials blamed for recent clashes between their rival parties in a key northwest province.

The two premiers, whose relations have grown increasingly strained since they formed an uneasy coalition government after U.N.-supervised elections in 1993, signed an agreement on Sunday night to recall at least two senior officials from each of their parties in the main rice-growing province of Battambang.
Prak Sokann, advisor to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, confirmed the agreement but said he had no more details.
A senior Interior Ministry official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters that "four people will be brought to come to work in Phnom Penh temporarily."

He said they included Battambang Governor Ung Samy and regional military commander Hul Savoeun of Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party, and Deputy Governor Serei Kosal of Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party.
The official said one other senior FUNCINPEC official from the northwest province was being recalled but he was not sure who.
The officials could not be immediately reached for comment but sources said a delegation of officials from both parties, including the co-defence ministers, was sent to Battambang on Monday.
Co-Defence Ministers Tea Banh of the CPP and Tea Chamrath of FUNCINPEC flew to Battambang on Friday to defuse tensions and order troops loyal to each party to pull back after recent violent clashes.
Analysts said tensions would ease with the removal of Ung Samy and Serei Kosal, whose personal feud had kept temperatures high in the province and triggered clashes last November.

Their rivalry reflected relations in the ruling coalition, which have hit a low since Ranariddh threatened last March to leave the government unless his party was given a greater share of power to reflect its narrow 1993 polls win.
Strained ties have been exacerbated by rival bids by the two premiers to win the allegiance of thousands of defectors from the Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement in recent months.
The premiers were seen embracing and chatting on Monday while waiting at Phnom Penh's international airport for the arrival of Indonesian President Suharto on a three-day state visit.
